name: Qatayef with Walnuts
instructions: Blend the flour, semolina, sugar, baking powder, yeast, and water until smooth, then let the batter rest for 15 minutes.
Cook small circles of batter on a nonstick pan on one side only until the tops are dry.
Mix the walnuts with 2 tablespoons of sugar and cinnamon, then fill and fold each qatayef, pinching the edges closed.
Brush with butter and bake at 375°F for 12–15 minutes, until golden.
For the syrup, boil 1 cup sugar, ½ cup water, and lemon juice for 5 to 7 minutes, then pour over the warm qatayef.
story: Qatayef is especially sweet to me because it reminds me of Ramadan and the evenings I spent with my family after breaking our fast. It was something I always looked forward to during the month. I chose this dessert because to me it represents more than just food it reminds me of family, togetherness, and the warmth of Ramadan.
